prompt:
Style: a texture sheet for a first-person 3D game on a 1994 DOS PC with a 256-colour VGA palette. Sixteen square surface textures arranged in an exact 4 by 4 grid of equal squares, separated by straight, even gutters of pure black (#000000), with a pure black border around the whole sheet. Every square is filled edge to edge with one flat surface material, seen straight on (orthographic, no perspective, no frame, no vignette). The textures are made the way textures for mid-1990s software-rendered PC games were made: digitized photographs of real materials, retouched by hand, that will be reduced to 64 by 64 pixels and one shared 256-colour palette. So they need crisp, high-contrast, chunky mid-scale detail (big stones, wide planks, deep dark joints and cracks), gritty and a little grimy, with plenty of dark values, no smooth gradients, no fine noise that would vanish when reduced. Flat, even, frontal lighting: no cast shadows, no highlights, no light direction, no darkened edges (the game darkens the textures itself). Unless a square says otherwise, each texture tiles seamlessly left/right and top/bottom, with even brightness across the square.
Row 1, left to right: (1) quay paving seen from above: rounded grey granite setts laid in straight horizontal rows, dark gaps between them; (2) harbour quay wall: large dressed grey granite blocks in four horizontal courses, dark mortar joints; (3) cottage wall: rough irregular grey-brown fieldstones with pale lime mortar; (4) dark blue-grey slate roof tiles in overlapping horizontal rows.
Row 2: (5) weathered grey-brown wooden deck planks running horizontally, dark gaps, a few nail heads; (6) dark tarred wooden boards running vertically, almost black-brown, with iron bolts; (7) weathered whitewashed lime plaster, off-white with grey stains and small cracks; (8) dark coastal cliff rock with deep cracks and ledges, grey-brown.
Row 3: (9) short coarse grass and moss with a few small stones, muted olive green, seen from above; (10) one side of a wooden cargo crate filling the square exactly: a frame of dark boards around lighter horizontal planks with one diagonal brace (not tiling); (11) weathered white-painted overlapping boat planks running horizontally, dark seams, chipped paint; (12) dark red-brown bricks in courses with grey mortar.
Row 4: (13) one old wooden plank door with two black iron strap hinges, filling the square (not tiling); (14) one small four-pane window glowing warm yellow from inside, dark wooden frame and cross bars, filling the square (not tiling); (15) dark riveted iron plate, brown-grey with rust patches and rows of rivets; (16) wet granite blocks at the waterline: dark grey blocks with green seaweed and black algae.
The materials are for a small stone fishing harbour on a fictional island in a northern sea (only the materials, not the scene).
No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.
Image format: square 1:1.
